summary: Stable and development release channels: a dev branch beside main; the Release workflow (both forge copies) publishes main as stable and dev as a development pre-release (vX.Y.Z-dev.N, Debian X.Y.Z~dev.N) into its own APT subtree (/apt/dev), download tree (/downloads/dev) and Gitea pre-release with the newest three kept, and never deploys the website; release-version.py numbers development builds, release-publish.py orders them numerically, apt-publish.py and gitea-release.py gain retention; phase1, image and github checks also run on dev pushes; development package, appliance and Controller builds default to the dev archive subtree; a package-edition host takes a stable or dev channel (the archive root or its dev subdirectory) through the existing host-local PUT /api/local/v1/updates/settings; an Update channel picker appears on each image host's card in Controller Settings, Updates and on the host-local Updates page.

guide.reason: Operators now choose a channel and maintainers publish to two channels; both pages describe the selectors, the development archive and downloads, the version numbering, the retention and the troubleshooting. They state that the selectors were not walked through.

api.reason: Host-local PUT /api/local/v1/updates/settings is now also answered by the package edition (channel stable or dev, no base_url; 400 invalid_channel and invalid_base_url, 409 settings_overridden while NEX_UPDATE_REPO fixes the archive) and GET /api/local/v1/updates of a package host adds UpdateStatus.channel. No new route, no Controller route or managed command change: the Controller UI uses the existing settings relay for image hosts, and package hosts are not relayed. An older Core answers the package-edition PUT with 409 unsupported_edition.

roadmap.reason: Release and update plumbing for development builds; no roadmap milestone changed status.

state.reason: A host's channel is Core state on that host and the Controller keeps nothing: the picker only asks the host to change it and shows what the host reports. The release side keeps its state on the publishing host (the APT and download trees) and in Gitea releases, not in the Controller.
state.record: Host-local /etc/nex/updates.conf: channel= (image edition, reported in Inventory.image.channel) or repo_url (package edition: the archive root, or the root plus /dev for the development channel). A fresh Controller reads the image edition's channel from each host's next report with the same value; package-edition hosts are not relayed and need nothing recovered.

verification.method: python3 -m unittest discover -s tests -p 'test_*.py' (644 of 646 pass; the one failure, test_host_tool_isolation, comes from the unfinished image-update work that makes internal/controller reach vmhost, not from this change); go test of ./internal/nexupdate ./internal/localcore ./internal/controller ./internal/protocol; web channel and image-updates tests and tsc --noEmit; scripts/generate_api.py --check and tests/test_api_contract.py. The release workflow steps ran for real under bash against recording stand-ins for ssh, scp and python3, and the reachability step against a local HTTP server. Not run: a forge release, the website host, an apt client, a browser walkthrough, the website build and any package or appliance build.
